# pull and git stash pop

Fix `pull` popping a stash it did not create:

```
1. git stash is present
2. nothing to stash
3. pull
4. git stash pop up unreleated stash
```

The stash-then-pop wrapper ([[DOT-189]]) ran `git stash pop` unconditionally; when the working tree was clean, `git stash` saved nothing, and the pop afterwards applied whatever older entry sat on top of the stash list — silently mixing unrelated changes into the freshly pulled tree.

Expected: pop only what this `pull` stashed; a clean tree means no stash and no pop.

<!-- 2026-09-16T05:49Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/198#issuecomment-5711688142
Code vs intent: fixed for the "nothing stashed" case, but the pop still happens via an EXIT trap (see the note on #190); in bash a second dirty `pull` in the same session replaces the first trap, so only one pop ever runs.
